Candidate-averaged BCE is L=[softplus(−s⁺)+Σ softplus(s⁻)]/(K+1), giving logit gradients (σ(s⁺)−1)/(K+1) and σ(s⁻)/(K+1). At zero logits, K=16 gives positive −1/34, each negative +1/34: aggregate negative pressure is 16 times positive pressure. Increasing K weakens the positive contribution while aggregate negative pressure approaches a constant. gBCE multiplies only the positive term/gradient by β=1−t+tK/(|I|−1); β=1 recovers BCE. Thus calibration changes relative weighting, not merely global scale; K and catalog size also affect β. These gradients follow directly from the [authors’ loss definitions](https://github.com/asash/gsasrec).

Candidate softmax uses L=−s⁺+logsumexp(s⁺,s⁻₁,…,s⁻ₖ), with gradients p⁺−1 and p⁻ⱼ. Positive and aggregate negative gradients always balance; negatives compete, emphasizing higher-scoring candidates. At equal logits with K=16, gradients are −16/17 and +1/17 each: versus averaged BCE, positive magnitude is 32× and each negative 2×. No scalar multiplier reconciles both. These are derived logit gradients, not guaranteed parameter-update ratios. Increasing K changes competition and sampled difficulty; candidate softmax is not automatically full-catalog softmax. [Sampled objective definition](https://github.com/antklen/sasrec-bert4rec-recsys23).

Recommended controls: preserve BERT4Rec masks, initialization, batches, negative draws, reduction over valid targets, and training/evaluation budgets. Compare raw objectives, scalar-rescaled BCE, positive-reweighted BCE, and per-objective learning-rate sweeps. Log positive/negative gradient contributions, parameter-gradient norms, clipping frequency and actual update norms. Adam’s normalization complicates loss-scale/LR equivalence. Keep K=16 initially; then vary K, declaring whether β or t stays fixed. Identical optimizer settings alone cannot establish objective superiority.
